stem: An 84-year-old man has had 5 days of constipation and a swollen abdomen. He has no fever and has never had abdominal surgery. A tender 3-cm lump in the right groin cannot be pushed back into the abdomen, and gurgling sounds are heard over it.
oneliner: 84M + 5 days of constipation + distended abdomen + tender irreducible right groin lump + bowel sounds over it → which complication follows if untreated?
ask: If the groin lump is left untreated, which of the following complications is most likely?

options.A: Twisting of the colon around its mesentery
options.B: Ischemic necrosis of the trapped bowel loop
options.C: Telescoping of one bowel segment into the next
options.D: Fibrous bands forming between bowel loops
options.E: Embolic occlusion of the superior mesenteric artery

whyNot.A: Volvulus does not need a **groin lump**; his obstruction is explained by the **irreducible groin mass** with bowel sounds
whyNot.C: Mainly a problem of **children** and it does not form a **groin lump**; he is 84
whyNot.D: Adhesions follow earlier abdominal surgery, and he has **never had abdominal surgery**; they also would not make a **groin lump**
whyNot.E: Causes sudden severe pain; his picture is **days of constipation, distention and a groin lump**

answer: Ischemic necrosis of the trapped bowel loop
why: An **irreducible, tender groin mass containing bowel** with obstruction is an incarcerated hernia. The neck of the sac squeezes the loop, venous and then arterial flow fall, and the **bowel becomes ischemic and necrotic (strangulation)**.
chain: A bowel loop enters the sac and cannot return (incarceration)
The neck of the sac squeezes the loop; venous then arterial flow falls

idea.rule: A hernia that will not reduce is dangerous because the neck of the sac compresses the blood supply of its contents.
also: Femoral hernias strangulate most often because of their narrow neck
Fever, skin redness and a very tender lump suggest strangulation
Richter hernia traps only part of the bowel wall and can strangulate without obstruction
Strangulation needs urgent surgery, with resection of necrotic bowel

stem: A 56-year-old man with alcohol-related cirrhosis has had two episodes of bleeding from esophageal varices despite banding and propranolol. A stent is placed through the jugular vein to connect a branch of the portal vein with a hepatic vein. Three weeks later his wife brings him in because he is sleepy at midday, forgetful, and has a flapping tremor of both hands when his arms are held out. He has no fever, abdominal pain or vomiting of blood. Urine output and creatinine are unchanged.
oneliner: 56M + alcohol-related cirrhosis + recurrent variceal bleeding + stent from portal to hepatic vein 3 weeks ago + sleepiness, forgetfulness, flapping tremor + no fever, pain, hematemesis + creatinine unchanged → which complication follows the shunt?
ask: Which of the following complications of the procedure most likely explains these findings?

whyNot.A: Presents with **fever and abdominal pain**; he has **neither**
whyNot.B: Shows **falling urine output and rising creatinine**; his are **unchanged**
whyNot.C: Causes abdominal pain and ascites; he has **no abdominal pain** and his picture is **sleepiness and a flapping tremor**
whyNot.E: He has **no vomiting of blood**, and the stent was placed to lower portal pressure

why: The stent diverts **portal blood around the liver**, so gut-derived ammonia escapes hepatic clearance. **New sleepiness, forgetfulness and asterixis** after the shunt mean hepatic encephalopathy.
chain: The stent connects the portal vein to a hepatic vein
Gut-derived ammonia is not cleared by hepatocytes
Ammonia reaches the brain and astrocytes swell

idea.rule: Any portosystemic shunt, surgical or by stent, lets gut-derived ammonia bypass the liver, so encephalopathy is the cost of lower portal pressure.
also: Triggers: gastrointestinal bleeding, infection, constipation, sedatives and low potassium
Spontaneous portosystemic shunts in cirrhosis cause encephalopathy the same way
Asterixis is a flapping tremor of outstretched hands
